attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps the 'every single' scope, the hundreds-of-millions-or-billions scale and the 'seem to lose it' hedge. It is framed as an observation, but the universal is hyperbole and the loss part is only an impression.

contract.note: The contract rightly notes that 'major' institutions are an undefined set, that 'take forever' has no measure, and that 'seem' is a hedge. It treats the claim as untestable rather than stretching it either way.

evidence.note: Dated before the evaluation date. It shows many large banks in a $38B data center loan, which fits the broad financing theme. It does not establish 'every single' institution or any project losses.

reviews.rationale: The universal 'every single major bank and financial institution' names no defined set. 'Take forever' has no measure, and 'only seem to lose it' is a hedged impression. The packet shows heavy bank lending to data centers, which is context only. Nothing could fairly settle the universal or the loss impression, so the claim is not scorable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence, his commentary following a block he quotes from his earlier writing.

semantics.note: 'These companies' correctly names Cursor, Perplexity, Cognition and Cohere. The profitability part is present tense. 'No path to an acquisition or IPO' is in substance an unqualified claim that none will exit, so it works as a forecast, which matches the contract's axis.

contract.note: Plain reading is fair and ordinary: a completed full acquisition months later shows a path existed. The contract honours his caveat about all-stock and acquihire deals by requiring a full purchase with liquid stock.

evidence.note: CNBC, 2026-06-16: SpaceX, newly listed on Nasdaq, signed an agreement to buy Cursor outright for $60B in stock.
TechCrunch, 2026-08-15: the Cursor acquisition closed. This is a completed full acquisition and meets the early-resolution rule.

reviews.rationale: The claim joins two parts and both must hold. SpaceX, by then publicly traded, closed a full $60B acquisition of Cursor on 2026-08-15, before the evaluation date. That meets the early-resolution rule, so the 'no path' part fails. Profitability is not settled by the packet, but the conjunction is contradicted either way.
